rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 6 replicated the iteration 1 design exactly (score 75.9694, identical per-track metrics), so the 0.29 s-bend progress is reproducible for this design and seed set, not luck. The remaining problem is the s-bend, where steering_oscillation is 0.23 and line_loss_events is about 1.95, and the slalom, where line_loss_events is 2.0. Every track still ends off_track with max_error about 0.061 to 0.065, just above the 0.06 m limit. Earlier single-lever tests moved progress in ways that tie to the controller. kd 0.1 (iterations 2 and 3) cut s-bend and oval progress, while kd 0.2 (iteration 1) kept it. Iteration 2 (base 1.2) and iteration 3 (kp 2.5) showed that speed and kp do not move max_error. Sensor spacing and footprint changes (iterations 4 and 5) cut progress without moving max_error.

Change. I keep the replicated iteration 1 design and change one lever: kd from 0.2 to 0.15, the midpoint the Evaluator asked me to check. Everything else is unchanged: base_speed 1.4, kp 2.0, ki 0, weights -2..2, sensors at x -0.02..0.02 with y 0.04, sensor_size 0.012, and last_direction line loss. Geometry is also unchanged.

Why. kd 0.2 gave the oscillation peak (0.23 on the s-bend). kd 0.1 cut progress. Under the iteration 1 baseline, kd 0.15 should cut jitter while keeping most of the progress.

Expected result. steering_oscillation on the s-bend falls from about 0.23 to about 0.18 to 0.20. Progress stays between about 0.25 and 0.29 on the s-bend and near 0.16 on the oval. Score is near 76, with a chance of a small gain if line losses fall. max_error is probably still near 0.06 to 0.065.

Hypotheses. (H1) kd 0.15 keeps s-bend progress at or above 0.25 while cutting oscillation below 0.20. (H2) If progress falls below about 0.22, the progress lost by kd is the limit, and the next lever is kp with kd 0.2 kept. (H3) max_error stays about 0.06 to 0.065, so the remaining error is set by bend geometry and reach, not by a gain. Measurements wanted are progress, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, and max_error with its location.
